author: Mark Atwood
text: worker7 pass-3 evidence (no code changed): the fork is confirmed three-way and corpus-invisible. C test_decap_expired_shadow (lichen/tests/tunnel_auth/src/main.c:219-261) pins skip-expired-permit-shorter; Rust test expired_longest_prefix_denies_without_falling_back_to_shorter_live_grant (rust/lichen-gateway/tests/tunnel_auth_vectors.rs:412-422) pins select-then-expire-deny; Python tunnel_auth.py:548-554 matches Rust. Additional data points for adjudication: (1) spec 06-security.md 8.11 data-plane rule is silent on overlapping grants ('If missing or expired: drop'); (2) both semantics are defensible as fail-closed (C: deny unless some LIVE grant covers; Rust/Py: lapsed longest grant vets the packet = deny) - this is a policy choice, not a correctness bug, and deciding it unilaterally would be silently picking a side; (3) the pre-fix C behavior (shadow-deny) has a live survivor in Rust today, so '7e39bf4655 was a plain bugfix' is contestable: worker6-3lk7 bead no longer exists in the store to cite its rationale; (4) second, smaller fork adjacent: tie-break on equal prefix_len differs - Rust picks least-recently-used (tunnel_auth.rs:439-442), C keeps first-in-table (tunnel_auth.c:472), Python max() is insertion-order-dependent; and (5) denial-precedence order differs for multiply-invalid inputs (C verifies signature before egress binding; Rust egress before signature; decap: Rust checks source/dest scope before route validity, C/Python check route first, scope after grant match) - wire code is 4.03 either way, but the shared corpus pins no ordering for compound-invalid cases. Recommend: human ADJUDICATE (a) vs (b), then add corpus cases expired_longest_live_shorter + equal_prefix_tie + compound-invalid precedence so the choice cannot re-fork.
